summary: Revise at 6.8, up from 6.3 in round 1. Caiman scores 7.0 and the ship bar is 7.5; on the calibration scale this ties Kraken's round-2 level and sits under Basiliscus (7.2, cut). Every gate in report.json is green at draft and export. The template gate is now recorded and passes: 1 design.set patch, 874,982 bytes against the 1 MB stock budget, and a cold evaluation identical in source and mesh. Of round 1's 8 punch items, 3 are met (7 template, 8 sand slots, and the band-centring part of 1). 3 are partly met (1 fleur, 3 shank, 6 arcade) and 2 are not met (4 border, 5 legend depth). The big win is the fleur. Its band is now centred, and hero-300 and face-300 read 'fleur-de-lis in a Gothic quatrefoil seal' instead of 'knot'. The cheek arcade is now five clean pointed lancets with smooth flanks (side.png, cheek-close.png). The weaknesses have moved down the ring. The new shank 'arcade' is 28 bench slots straddling the crown-to-wall edge, and at hero and 300 px they read as knurling or gear teeth, not lancets. The shoulder roundels are plain overlapping round dimples, a bubble chain with no foils. The shoulder window's lights and hood are still open-ended outlines with no sill. The table work also has open items. The 12-foil border is still round scallops; its cusp points are too small to count at 300 px. The legend was cut at 0.20 mm, not the 0.35-0.40 asked, and still washes out in the hero highlight. The fleur is a kit of unjoined parts: a sausage centre petal, two crescent side petals, and three faceted leaf blobs under the band. Round 3 is the last. It can reach 7.5 only if it fixes the shank, shoulder and border reads together with the fleur's joins.
strengths: The fleur now reads as a fleur-de-lis at 300 px (face-300.png, hero-300.png). Its band is centred on the axis, and it was cut at 0.60 mm, so it holds a strong dark floor.

The cheek arcade (side.png, cheek-close.png) is five crisp equilateral pointed lancets at sink 0.50, along_pull. Round 1's sawtooth flanks are gone. This is the best architectural passage on the ring.
The face remains a credible Gothic seal matrix: a pointed quatrefoil, a mirrored minuscule Textura legend with a cross pattée, a ruled band and a cusped rim, filling the table edge to edge.

Ornament now runs from the table to within about 25 deg of the palm on both sides (Shank arcade, right 22.5 to 295 deg; left 157.5 to 245 deg), graded from 1.00 x 2.60 down to 0.75 x 1.96 mm. Round 1's 60% bare stock is gone.

The process is honest. The seal and shank are bench cuts, and the arcade and roundels are cast along the pull. 017's hard table-to-wall angle is intact (bare-vs-finished.png), with 0.011 mm of envelope fill. The sand slots are now 0.40 to 0.50 mm, above the 0.30 Delft detail.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: The coverage is now continuous: table, cheek arcade, shoulder window and roundels, then a shank chain to about 25 deg from the palm. The theme still breaks below the cheeks. The shank slots read as knurled or ribbed edging (hero.png right shank, reverse.png, palm.png), the roundels as a bubble chain, and the window as an unfinished outline. Below the table it reads as three unrelated vocabularies, not one chapter house.

checklist.item: Reads as its Gothic subject at 300 px without the caption
checklist.reason: face-300 reads 'Gothic seal: fleur-de-lis in a quatrefoil with a blackletter legend'. hero-300 now names the fleur, and the near cheek lancets are visible. It does not read as a perforated or grooved band, although the shank alone would.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines: crisp, no combing, smearing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: The arcade is fixed. Failures remain: (1) stones.png and cheek-close.png show the fleur foot as three faceted, smeared leaf blobs, and the centre petal, side petals, band and foot float as separate pieces with no joins; (2) the shoulder roundels (side.png, reverse.png) are overlapping plain discs with no foils, and they merge; (3) the shoulder window's hood is an open curve and its two lights are open-bottomed strokes (shoulder-close.png); (4) the legend letter walls and border rings show stepped, polygonal edges in cheek-close.png.

checklist.item: Stones in made settings, à jour, coloured as stained glass
checklist.reason: Not applicable. The concept carries no stones; stones.json is empty and the previewed count is 0.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms are sculpted
checklist.reason: The 28 shank slots are identical straight-sided notches cut through the crown edge. They read as a machined knurl (contact-300 bottom-left and bottom-right, palm.png). The window is a wire outline. Every cut below the table is flat-floored with no moulding. The ring has no modelled form anywhere.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: bare-vs-finished.png: 017's table edge and wall angles are intact; envelope fill is 0.011 mm at 129.5 deg.

checklist.item: Distinct silhouette; custom heads at least 13 mm; shoulder ornament not cut off before the face
checklist.reason: Factory 017 at 16 x 15.6 mm. It is the only plain cushion signet in Tenebrae, so its silhouette is distinct. The shoulder ornament runs into the cheek arcade without a gap.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: Density is now near Caiman's from face to shank. There is still no large form: everything is shallow intaglio of 0.2 to 0.6 mm on stock polish. Legibility below the table is under Caiman's. Its worked scales read at every angle, while Sigillum's shank and shoulders do not read as architecture.

gates.verified: verification.json and report.template_gate: 1 patch (/manufacturing, node 430), template 874,982 B against the 1,000,000 B stock budget, source_identical, cold design and graph reload true, template_gate_passed true

punch_list.zone: Shank crown edges, stamps 'Shank arcade, right 1-14' (22.5 to 295 deg) and 'left 1-14' (157.5 to 245 deg)
punch_list.change: Make the shank chain read as Gothic arches, not knurling. Move the lancets off the crown-to-wall edge onto the flat ±z side walls, inset at least 0.4 mm from the edge so each arch is a closed outline; the slots now break through the edge, leaving open notches. Give each a true equilateral pointed head (the cheek-arcade outline scaled down) and a sill, and cut 7 to 9 per side at about 1.2 x 2.2 mm, graded to 0.9 x 1.6 toward the palm, rather than 14 at 0.75-1.0 mm wide. Keep 0.4-0.5 mm piers between them. If they stay on the side walls, cast them along_pull at sink 0.35; else keep bench.
punch_list.acceptance: hero.png and reverse.png: each shank lancet shows a closed pointed head and a sill, set inside the wall with polished metal between it and the crown edge. contact-300 bottom row: the shank reads 'row of arches', not 'ribbed, knurled or gear-toothed edge'.

punch_list.zone: Shoulders: stamps 'Shoulder window, right/left' (hood, lights, oculus; 37 and 143 deg) and 'Shoulder roundel 1/2, right/left 1-3' (33.6 to 44.5 deg and 135.5 to 146.4 deg)
punch_list.change: Window (round 1 item 2, still open): close every outline. The hood must meet a sill line at its foot, and each light must be a closed pointed lancet (about 1.0 x 2.6 mm) with a 0.5 mm mullion left proud between them. The oculus must be a closed cusped circle about Ø 1.0 above the lights. Roundels: the three discs overlap and read as bubbles. Space them so their edges are 0.4 mm or more apart and grade them Ø 2.0 / 1.6 / 1.2. Give each a crisp quatrefoil, or at minimum a cusped circle with 4 points at least 0.3 mm deep. A plain circle does not pass.
punch_list.acceptance: shoulder-close.png: the window shows a closed arch, two closed lights, a mullion, an oculus and a sill, with no line ending in open field. side.png and reverse.png: three separate roundels per shoulder side, each showing four foils or four cusp points.

punch_list.zone: Table centre: stamps 'Seal fleur, centre petal / left petal / right petal / foot / band'
punch_list.change: Join the fleur into one figure (round 1 item 1, remaining half). The centre petal is a round-ended sausage. Redraw it as a lanceolate petal with a pointed tip, widest at about 40% of its height, whose base runs into the band. The side petals must spring from the band ends and from the centre petal's base, not float as crescents; curl their tips outward and down. Replace the three faceted leaf blobs of the foot with three smooth closed lobes, joined to the band's underside. The centre lobe should be about 1.3 mm tall, the side lobes 0.9 mm, with outline resolution high enough that no facets show. Keep sink 0.60.
punch_list.acceptance: stones.png: the fleur is one continuous silhouette; no petal, foot lobe or band is separated by uncut field, and the foot shows no faceted or smeared edges. face-300.png: the fleur reads as a classic fleur-de-lis, not a bar crossed by a stick.

punch_list.zone: Table rim: stamps 'Cusped border, foil 1-12, *' and 'Cusped border, point 1-12'
punch_list.change: Round 1 item 4 is still open. The 12 foils remain rounded scallops, and the points are tiny spurs. Draw each foil as a pointed arc pair meeting the next foil at an inward cusp that projects at least 0.6 mm toward the legend, ending in a sharp point. Or halve to 8 larger pointed foils. Cut the border at 0.30 mm, not 0.20.
punch_list.acceptance: face-300.png: 12 (or 8) sharp inward points are countable round the rim, and it no longer reads as a scalloped coin or bottle-cap edge.

punch_list.change: Round 1 item 5 is still open. Cut the legend at 0.35-0.40 mm as the concept specifies, and the quatrefoil rules at 0.30. Raise the letter outline resolution so the letter walls are clean curves. cheek-close.png now shows polygonal, stepped walls on letters and border rings.
punch_list.acceptance: hero.png: every legend letter, including 'cathedralis' in the upper-right highlight, shows a dark floor. cheek-close.png: letter and ring walls show no polygon facets or steps.

punch_list.change: Round 1 item 6, the height half. The lancets are still 1.99 to 2.78 mm tall, with the centre bay the shortest. Raise all five to about 3.0-3.2 mm and level their sills, or grade them symmetrically with the centre the tallest, like a chapter-house arcade.
punch_list.acceptance: side.png: five lancets with level sills, the centre one at least as tall as its neighbours, filling about 80% of the cheek height.

punch_list.zone: Bore lip under the table, theta about 60-120 (palm.png, inner upper edge)
punch_list.change: palm.png shows a ragged, torn-looking edge where the bore meets the underside of the head. Check whether it comes from stock or from the sand-master envelope. If it is a build artefact, raise the local resolution or smooth it.
punch_list.acceptance: palm.png: the bore's upper inner edge is one smooth line, with no serrations.
